about: Derived-check findings that are intentional. Each entry names its check id and finding key exactly as scripts/parity-check.mjs prints them, and says why. An entry that no longer matches anything is reported as stale: delete it.

entries.reason: By the section's own notes the Mac's JSONEncoder writes an equivalent seed body, not the same bytes, so it doesn't assert this vector.
Linux writes the seed through the Node CLI's appliance-provision, which packages/flagship-builder/tests/appliance.test.ts checks against this section.

flagship/boot/v1 is the phones' BAK challenge signature in BootAuthorization, which no server code verifies; the webapp's boot approval signs flagship/boot-auth/v1 (bootApproval.js).

Pairing a phone with Studio (desktop installer) is phone-only; the webapp never pairs Studio.
Phones re-verify the box's STK-signed report to pin its certificate fingerprint; a browser has no API to pin a certificate.
iOS's IRK-signed reconcile read; Android and the webapp reconcile pending servers from the unauthenticated /pods pending[] list (PendingServerReconciler.kt).

The native default PRF salt; the webapp's passkey recovery derives its PRF salt from the user's passphrase (Argon2id in the recovery sub-origin).
iOS's slash-form app-backup SWK (Keystore.deriveSWK) is not used by any other client; Android and the webapp derive the dotted protocol SWK (ServerKeys.deriveSwk).
No client offers one-off voi.ci short links: iOS and Android carry only the unused canonical-bytes primitive, and the webapp has no such screen.
